messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — GCP asia-east1 Cloud Router BGP flapping detected. Severity: P1. Symptoms: private Interconnect/VPN routes intermittently withdrawn, packet loss ~20% between on-prem and VPCs, several customer streams failing. Affected: 3 Dedicated customers + 1 Private deployment in APAC. Links: https://monitoring.internal/gcp/cloudrouter/asia-east1 (metric spike). Paging @Amelia Chen (oncall).

Amelia Chen: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Starting triage now and following the 'cloud-router-bgp-flap' runbook: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/cloud-router-bgp-flap.

Amelia Chen: Quick check — running BGP status against the affected Cloud Router.
```bash
gcloud compute routers get-status cr-asia-east1-01 --region asia-east1 --format json | jq '.bgpPeers[] | {name: .name, sessionState: .sessionState, lastEvent: .lastBgpEvent}'
# output: 
# {"name":"peer-onprem-1","sessionState":"IDLE","lastEvent":"flap: 2026-03-15T02:04:12Z"}
# {"name":"peer-onprem-2","sessionState":"ESTABLISHED","lastEvent":"none"}
```

Kyung Park: Seeing frequent BGP NOTIFICATION/UPDATE churn on GCP side. Also ECMP shifts on egress paths — likely upstream fabric instability. We should: 1) move traffic to secondary Interconnect VLAN attachment (if available) for affected customers, 2) temporarily withdraw large custom route advertisements to reduce churn.

Mohit Patel: I'm on the VLAN failover. Changing attachment for cust-dedicated-3 to the standby attachment now. Running: 
```bash
gcloud compute interconnects attachments update vlan-att-123 --region asia-east1 --router cr-asia-east1-01 --operation failover
```
(That script sets local preference to prefer standby attachment).

Amelia Chen: Traceroute from on-prem to a failing customer endpoint shows blackhole at cloud-router ASN 64512.
```text
traceroute to 10.8.4.2 (10.8.4.2), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  gw-onprem  0.7 ms 0.6 ms 0.6 ms
 2  core-peering  3.2 ms 3.1 ms 3.0 ms
 3  cr-asia-east1-01 (35.190.10.1)  *  *  *
```

Amelia Chen: I've opened a GCP Support case: CASE-20260315-4821. Requested immediate fabric-side investigation and BGP session trace.

Raj Nair: CS — any customers already impacted who need an immediate status update? We should send an interim note.

Amelia Chen: Yes, 3 Dedicated customers are reporting RPC failures and one Private deployment has degraded API response times (~3–4x p99). Drafting a customer-facing summary now: "We are actively investigating intermittent connectivity between your on-prem network and our APAC private endpoints caused by a flapping BGP session in GCP asia-east1. Mitigation steps in progress include failover to secondary Interconnect attachments and route dampening. We'll update in 30 minutes or on stabilization." Thoughts?

Raj Nair: LGTM. Can you include expected ETA for next update (30min) and impacted resources (VLAN IDs, router names)? Customers like explicit identifiers.

Amelia Chen: Good call — adding VLAN IDs and router names. Posting update to all affected customers in 10.

Kyung Park: GCP support responded — they see 'control-plane maintenance' with flaps on that PoP. They recommend: 1) withdraw large optional route advertisements to reduce convergence, 2) prefer alternate path via standby attachment, 3) hold config changes that might re-trigger session resets. I'm going to prepare a withdraw script for non-essential custom routes.

Mohit Patel: Standby attachment failover completed for cust-dedicated-3. Monitoring traffic now. Packet loss for that tenant dropped from ~22% to ~1.2% within 90s.

Amelia Chen: Confirming metrics:
- cust-dedicated-3: packet_loss p95 -> 1.2% (was 22%)
- cust-dedicated-1,2: still showing intermittent withdraws, we're applying route withdraw for non-critical /24s now.

infra-bot: Automated note: applied route-withdraw script to cr-asia-east1-01 at 2026-03-15T02:18:54Z by Mohit Patel (action id: a1b2c3).

Kyung Park: After withdrawing optional advertisements, BGP churn decreased significantly on GCP side. GCP engineer says they're seeing fewer NOTIFICATION messages. Recommend keeping withdrawals for 2–4 hours to ensure stability.

Amelia Chen: Update for customers posted. Case update to GCP submitted with logs. GCP support assigned engineer 'Li Wei' and escalated to networking tier-2.

Mohit Patel: Running tcpdump on router interface — seeing fewer BGP updates now. Sample: 
```text
20:19:30.123456 IP 10.100.0.1.179 > 35.190.10.1.179: Flags [P.], seq 1:245, ack 1, win 65535
# BGP UPDATE: withdrawn routes: none, advertised prefixes: reduced set
```

Amelia Chen: Preliminary mitigation looks effective. Customer impact reduced but not fully cleared for two tenants — will continue monitoring. If p99 stabilizes for 15m, we'll mark as mitigated.

Kyung Park: Recommending post-incident actions: 1) add automated failover play for Interconnect attachments in runbook, 2) ensure standby attachments are exercised monthly, 3) add dampening thresholds for Cloud Router route advertisements.

Amelia Chen: Agreed. Adding to action item list. Creating incident document in postmortems: https://incidents.internal/postmortems/1795001234.

Sara Kim: I'm next in rotation in ~40 minutes. Any outstanding actions I should pick up during handoff?

Amelia Chen: Handoff summary for Sara:
- Current state: BGP sessions largely stable; packet loss dropped to <1.5% for most tenants after failover/withdraw.
- Open items: keep route withdrawals for 2–4 hours, liaise with GCP Li Wei for confirmation of top-of-rack fabric health, runbook updates per Kyung's suggestions, coordinate long-term customer RTT verification with CS.
- Key links: CASE-20260315-4821, runbook link, postmortem draft.

Sara Kim: Got it. I'll monitor metrics and maintain customer comms if any regressions. If anything spikes, I'll ping Kyung directly.

Amelia Chen: Moving to monitoring-only. If stable for 15m, we'll change incident status to mitigated and keep as P1 in follow-up mode for RCA. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to MONITORING at 2026-03-15T02:42:20Z by Amelia Chen.

Amelia Chen: FINAL note before handoff — impact window: 02:03–02:38 UTC, primary cause: flapping BGP sessions on GCP asia-east1 PoP (under investigation by GCP). Mitigation: switched affected tenants to standby VLAN attachments and withdrew non-essential route advertisements. RCA follow-up and timeline to be posted in postmortem.

infra-bot: Created postmortem skeleton: /postmortems/1795001234 (assigned to Kyung Park).

Kyung Park: Acknowledged. I'll own the RCA and coordinate with GCP contacts.

Raj Nair: CS will send tailored impact emails to the affected customers now (includes VLAN IDs, router names, mitigation steps).

Amelia Chen: Handoff complete to Sara Kim. Signing off.

Sara Kim: Oncall pickup acknowledged. Monitoring.
